entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Diébédo Francis Kéré is a Burkinabé-German architect, recognized for creating innovative works that are often sustainable and collaborative in nature. In 2022, he became the first native African to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize. Educated at Technische Universität Berlin, he has lived in Berlin since 1985. Parallel to his studies, he established the Kéré Foundation, and in 2005 he founded Kéré Architecture. His architectural practice has been recognized internationally with awards including the Aga Khan Award for Architecture (2004) for his first building, the Gando Primary School in Burkina Faso, and the Global Holcim Award for Sustainable Construction.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the first native African to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 2022, Diébédo Francis Kéré's work has had a significant impact on the global architecture community, inspiring a new generation of sustainable and collaborative architects. His foundation has also provided critical support to education and healthcare initiatives in Burkina Faso.
